interpretation.reproduced: All five mappings have now been observed live on three separate occasions (2026-11-17 in the prior sessions, and twice on 2026-11-20 by sessions arena-23d7ed19 and arena-82d39deb). Every observation agrees, 5/5, so FLG-008 stays closed and the observed_* fields are reproducible rather than single-session noise. Across four separate observations on three dates — including two by sessions that had never seen the data — 5/5 tokens resolved to the same five ASINs, and all five page titles match the stored titles verbatim.
interpretation.what_reproduction_does_not_prove: Every final URL carries lv=shuf (shuffle) and plpRedirect=mhFallback (listing-page fallback). That is a fallback route, not a canonical resolution of the submitted token. The targets are stable per token across all three observations, so they are a usable observation — but they do not confirm that the person who supplied the links intended these five products. Intended fields therefore stay blank. Two of the four resolved URLs carried a variant parameter (th=1) on 2026-11-20, and Amazon's own rails showed sibling listings at other ASINs for three of the five products — so even a stable destination does not pin which colour, size or bundle a reader is served (FLG-026).
interpretation.operational_consequence: Keep publishing without reader links until the Associates one-link test (FLG-002) confirms destination and tracking report. If the owner confirms the five products are the intended ones, nothing about the pages changes except the intended_* fields and confirmation_date. Third observation also re-read each listing's product-details table: one recorded row was wrong (the 8-quart Chefman's wattage — FLG-022, corrected) and four listing-internal contradictions were confirmed (FLG-005, FLG-010, FLG-018, FLG-020).
